changes.title: Patterns of variable spikes can represent a value
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: Neural firing rates and spike variability supply the quantities needed for the later memory calculation. [Burak and Fiete (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1117386109) supply the Poisson network model. [Ben-Shushan et al. (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-29201-y) and [Mainali et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuron.2025.01.017) supply eye-control and spatial-coding context. The elementary numerical examples are guide-derived.

changes.title: Stable representations can accumulate error
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: A stable pattern of neural activity can retain a value while noise moves that value along a family of states. This is the continuous-memory setup of [Burak and Fiete (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1117386109). The two-variable illustrations are guide-derived.

changes.title: Spiking noise produces diffusion along the memory attractor
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Burak and Fiete (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1117386109) derive memory diffusion by projecting spike fluctuations through the network dynamics. The symmetric formula uses the authors' [2017 correction](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1706051114). Expanded projection examples are guide-derived.

changes.title: Boundaries and drift change memory error over long delays
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Burak and Fiete (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1117386109) explain long-delay behavior, angular boundaries, and state-dependent diffusion. These qualify how the central diffusion result can be used. The guide adds explicit boundary calculations and distinguishes its checks of other printed equations from the official correction.

changes.title: Spike information limits memory stability
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Burak and Fiete (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1117386109) relate the information in spikes to a lower bound on memory diffusion. The guide expands the proofs and labels its counterexamples and comparisons of fixed quantities.

changes.title: Readout accuracy depends on how a moving memory is observed
changes.role: central readout result and supporting extensions
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Burak and Fiete (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1117386109) derive limits on estimating a value that moves during observation. Partial access and alternative time scales extend that result. The guide supplies intermediate calculations and identifies source formulas needing qualification.

changes.title: Eye drift points to a shared neural drive
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Ben-Shushan et al. (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-29201-y) infer a substantial shared drive upstream of ocular motor neurons from recorded eye motion and spikes. The filter and covariance calculations explain the assumptions behind that inference.

changes.title: Drift growth distinguishes diffusion from filtered white noise
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Ben-Shushan et al. (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-29201-y) compare displacement statistics with the predictions of mechanical filtering and private motor noise. The one-filter calculation is a guide-derived teaching model, distinct from the full simulation.

changes.title: A noisy memory circuit can produce eye drift
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Ben-Shushan et al. (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-29201-y) show that a noisy integrator model can account for the motion after muscle filtering and delayed feedback. [Aksay et al. (2007)](https://doi.org/10.1038/nn1877) supply supporting circuit architecture. The match supports a possible source, rather than uniquely identifying it.

changes.title: Field counts and gaps reveal threshold and scale
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Mainali et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuron.2025.01.017) describe fields and gaps as regions of a smooth random input above or below threshold. Expanded crossing and parameter-inference calculations are guide-derived.

changes.title: High peaks explain size laws across dimensions
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Mainali et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuron.2025.01.017) derive dimension-dependent field-size statistics and compare them with recordings. The guide expands the local-peak derivation and separates limiting laws from finite-threshold behavior.

changes.title: Holes and measurements test the spatial explanation
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Mainali et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuron.2025.01.017) examine shapes, slices, and connectedness beyond the fitted summaries. The underlying recordings include [Eliav et al. (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abg4020), [Harland et al. (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2021.03.003), and [Yartsev and Ulanovsky (2013)](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1235338). Gaussian maps constrain possible inputs without uniquely identifying wiring.

changes.title: Spatial maps and memory dynamics need separate tests
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: The comparison joins the questions asked by [Burak and Fiete (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1117386109), [Ben-Shushan et al. (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-29201-y), and [Mainali et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuron.2025.01.017). Its common-displacement calculation and proposed joint experiment are developed here. The three papers did not jointly test that model.

changes.title: A stored weight and a remembered value are different states
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: von Neumann (1958) motivates the comparison. [Pehle et al. (2022)](https://doi.org/10.3389/fnins.2022.795876), Intel Labs (2021), Scholze et al. (2026), and [Le Gallo et al. (2023)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41928-023-01010-1) supply the architecture descriptions. Separating stored weights, changing neural states, and remembered values is the guide's organizing comparison.

changes.title: Discrete restoration and continuous drift produce different memory errors
changes.role: central neural distinction with supporting hardware examples
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Seung (1996)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.93.23.13339) and [Burak and Fiete (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1117386109) explain graded persistence and noise. [Massoud and Horiuchi (2011)](https://doi.org/10.1109/TCSI.2010.2055310) and [Giulioni et al. (2012)](https://doi.org/10.3389/fnins.2011.00149) supply distinct silicon demonstrations. The reduced feedback and error comparisons are guide-derived.

changes.title: Neuromorphic chips choose where physics performs the calculation
changes.role: central results of selected hardware studies
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Kleyko et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-55832-y) test temporal computation. [Aitsam et al. (2026)](https://doi.org/10.3389/fnins.2026.1910808) demonstrate persistent spatial activity. [Ortner et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-56345-4) study adaptation with phase-change computing. [Wang et al. (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-025-02361-0) study material-state stability. [Sun et al. (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42256-026-01255-3) evaluate a proposed dual-memory design. These results concern different kinds of memory, as the chapter explains.

changes.title: Memory experiments must separate device error from network dynamics
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: The proposed measurements combine the diffusion and readout questions of [Burak and Fiete (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1117386109), the output-filtering lesson of [Ben-Shushan et al. (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-29201-y), and the spatial-versus-temporal distinction exposed by [Mainali et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuron.2025.01.017). They are suggested tests, not a reported common hardware experiment.

changes.title: Network simulations test how random spikes move a stored value
changes.role: supporting simulations of a central theory
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Burak and Fiete (2012)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1117386109) compare stochastic network trajectories with their analytical diffusion prediction. The 2017 correction applies to Eq. 2. The simulations test the modeled dynamics, rather than measure memory errors in animals.

changes.title: Eye simulations connect a noisy neural command to measured motion
changes.role: model support for a central explanation
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Ben-Shushan et al. (2022)](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-29201-y) combine recorded-data analysis with a noisy integrator, motor neurons, muscles, and delayed feedback. Aksay et al. (2007) supply supporting circuit architecture. The generated signals test whether that mechanism can reproduce the measured statistics.

changes.title: Random spatial maps test the statistics of place fields
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: [Mainali et al. (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuron.2025.01.017) generate thresholded Gaussian spatial maps, fit selected summaries, and test additional field properties. Original animal recordings supply the comparison data. These are static-map simulations rather than recurrent memory dynamics.

changes.title: Reproduction depends on the model, numerical method, and measurement
changes.result_and_citations_retained_verbatim: The shared reproduction procedure is assembled here from the three studies. Author code is distinguished from optional numerical tools. No new full-paper reproduction is claimed.
